To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a relatively simple model that factors out detection scores, and encodes appearance and layout, can outperform existing state-of-the-art approaches on human-object interaction detection; and (2) training techniques that eliminate train-inference mismatch, reject easy negatives during mini- batch training, and use a ratio of negatives that is two orders larger than existing approaches can improve learning efficiency.

(i) a relatively simple model, trained with a novel training technique that eliminates train-inference mismatch, outperforms more complex approaches on human-object interaction detection; and (ii) a factorized model that encodes human-object appearance, coarse layout, and optionally fine-grain layout outperforms a model that does not factorize or encode layout.
